The land of five rivers in the northwest of South Asia, between the Indus and the Sutlej, shown on the map in 1492. Its main city is Lahore.

In 1492 Punjab was a province of the Delhi Sultanate under the Lodi dynasty, held by Afghan governors who often acted on their own. It was the road into India from the northwest: Timur had come this way to sack Delhi in 1398, and Babur would follow in the 1520s, founding the Mughal Empire.

These were also the years of Guru Nanak, who lived from 1469 to 1539, a Punjabi teacher whose message of one God beyond Hindu and Muslim rites became the root of Sikhism. Three centuries later Sikhs ruled Punjab themselves as the Sikh Empire. Under British rule the region grew rich on canals, and in 1947 it was split between India and Pakistan.
